ledger.note: 1336: Warangal is retaken. Kapaya 'took control of Warangal from Malik Maqbul in 1336' ('driving it out of Warangal in 1336') and held 'a wider swathe of eastern Telangana that was governed from there'; 'The Kakatiya empire came to an end in 1323 after the army of the Delhi sultanate invaded Warangal' (Reddy page, for context). The tughlaq-dynasty ledger has the matching loss of Warangal in 1336. [Repair 2026-10-20: the gain is now only the Warangal part; the Krishna-Godavari coast is Prolaya's earlier conquest.]
1336: the seat is Warangal. The page does not call Warangal the capital; it is the seat Kapaya won from the Sultanate.

1361: Golconda is ceded to the Bahmanis. Kapaya 'had to cede territory, including Golconda' after 'Several military engagements with Bahman Shah', and in 1361 gave Mohammed Shah I the Turquoise throne of Warangal in a treaty; the page gives no year for Golconda, so the treaty year is a bridging one. [Repair 2026-10-20: the Bahmani Sultanate page was opened for a date and does not give one: it says only 'It was a gift of Musunuri Kapaya Nayaka, a Telugu King in post-Kakateeya era' and, from Firishta, that on 23 March 1363 Mohammed Shah I sat on the Turquoise throne; the Musunuri page gives 1361 for the gift. Neither dates the cession of Golconda, so 1361 stays a bridging year at confidence 1.]

notes:
No Cliopatria row. Pages: Musunuri Nayaks, Recherla Nayaks (for the end). The Musunuri page gives no area, no capital and no date for the Golconda cession. Infobox 1335-1368 against Kapaya's reign 'c. 1333-1368' in the text and Prolaya's appearance c. 1330.
Not settled: the Hoysala appeal (Veera Ballala III, undated); the Reddis' exploitation (undated); the Recherla alliance; Krishna-Godavari holdings 'perhaps up to Rajahmundry'; whether the Bahmani held Golconda until 1368.
Counterparts: recherla-nayaks (written in this batch), bahmani-sultanate (sa-04-c), tughlaq-dynasty (sa-04-b), kakatiya-dynasty (sa-03), reddi-kingdom (this batch).
Gazetteer names needed: Rekapalle.

[Repair 2026-10-20, sa-04-x-fix] Region: the Vijayawada and Rajahmundry circles are cut along the north bank of the Krishna (12-point divider) and the shape stops at the Telangana line for the Recherla handover; the coast between the Krishna and the Godavari is Prolaya's conquest in the first keyframe and goes to nobody in 1368. The ruler strip is clipped to the 1335 start (Kapaya only; Prolaya has no reign years). Golconda: the Bahmani page was opened and dates only the throne (23 March 1363, Firishta) against the Musunuri page's 1361; the cession stays at 1361, confidence 1. Gazetteer names needed: Rekapalle, and 'Krishna-Godavari doab' for the divider.
